YOUR SIDE: # Draft appointment agreement **Parties.** Finch Review (“Finch”) and Noor agree to the following appointment. **1. Appointment and schedule.** Noor will serve as Head of the Methods Desk beginning on the date both parties have signed. Noor will work three fixed Finch days per week through March 31, 2027, and four fixed Finch days per week beginning April 1, 2027. Finch and Noor will record the weekdays in writing in advance. Any increase beyond four days requires mutual agreement. **2. Compensation.** The full-time salary basis is $125,000 per year. Noor’s salary is $75,000 annualized for the three-day schedule and rises automatically to $100,000 annualized on April 1, 2027. The April changes to schedule and salary apply regardless of the desk’s opening date. Compensation includes training and supervising the deputy as set out below. **3. Opening and deputy coverage.** The desk will take submissions on four fixed days each week beginning December 1, 2026. If either signing or the deputy’s appointment occurs after December 1, coverage will begin five working days after the later of signing and the deputy’s appointment. Finch is responsible for appointing the deputy and will identify the editor for recused matters in writing at signing. Before opening, Noor and the deputy will document the fourth-day procedure. During Noor’s three-day schedule, the deputy will acknowledge and log incoming submissions on the fourth day, triage them under the written criteria, and flag urgent matters to the duty editor that day. The deputy has no authority to decide corrections. Noor will train the deputy during scheduled Finch days and review the log and substantive recommendations on the next scheduled Finch day. Noor has no fourth-day on-call duty. **4. Intellectual property and outside-project carve-out.** Finch owns work Noor creates for the methods desk on Finch time. Noor may continue directing the existing editorial project identified in the disclosure under clause 5 until that project finishes. The outside project and its materials, including its data, drafts and unfinished articles, are expressly excluded from every Finch intellectual-property assignment, license and work-product provision applicable to this appointment. Those materials remain with the project. Finch acquires no ownership or license in them under this agreement. This carve-out controls over any inconsistent standard Finch provision. **5. Disclosure and recusal.** At signing, Noor will disclose in writing the outside project’s scope, funders and collaborators and will update the disclosure when they change. Noor will keep the two projects’ materials separate and will use no Finch resources or confidential submissions for the outside project. Noor will recuse from any Finch submission or correction involving the project, its data or its collaborators. The named Finch editor will handle that matter independently and exercise Noor’s authority under Schedule A throughout. **6. Editorial authority and review.** The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority subject to Schedule A, which forms part of this agreement. Nine months after the appointment begins, Finch and Noor will review desk performance, workload, time commitment, scope of the role and the operation of Schedule A. The review will cover the number of disputes and referrals, every referee outcome, every departure from a desk finding, and every decision to redact, defer or decline publication and its grounds. ## Schedule A — Methods corrections 1. **Standing authority.** Noor may determine whether a routine methods correction is warranted, settle its wording and clear it for publication. An author’s or editor’s objection alone does not suspend that authority. Finch retains control of acceptance decisions, scheduling, non-methods corrections and the non-methods elements of notices, subject to the publication deadlines below. 2. **Record and referral back.** When a methods correction is disputed, Noor will document the finding, supporting evidence and proposed wording. The editor-in-chief has five working days after receiving that record to refer the matter back to Noor once, giving specific written reasons. The author’s response may be included. If no referral is made within that period, the correction proceeds as cleared. 3. **Reconsideration and new evidence.** Noor will consider the referral in good faith and issue the desk’s final written finding and proposed wording within five working days, sooner if delay risks misleading readers. At any stage before publication, material new evidence must go to the desk first. Noor must consider it and reissue, revise or withdraw the finding before publication proceeds. 4. **Independent methods review.** Finch and Noor will jointly select an independent methods referee in advance. If the editor-in-chief still disputes the methods substance after reconsideration, they must identify the precise disputed claim and refer it with the full record within five working days of receiving Noor’s decision. Otherwise the correction proceeds as cleared. The referee will report to both parties within ten working days of referral. The ruling binds both parties on the accuracy of the disputed methods claim on the record reviewed. If the referee finds against the desk, Noor will withdraw or revise the statement accordingly. No correction will run on a claim the referee finds inaccurate. 5. **Publication after an upheld finding.** Finch will ordinarily publish the upheld methods statement on the article in Noor’s words within five working days of the ruling. The editor-in-chief authorizes the notice and controls its framing, context, placement and non-methods content. They may add a signed statement of their own. Finch may not substitute a contrary methods finding on the same record or attribute revised wording to the desk without Noor’s approval. 6. **Grounds and decision on publication.** The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority within the grounds agreed here. A decision to decline requires harm independent of the methods question. Permitted grounds are documented legal advice or a serious risk to the safety, privacy or confidentiality of an identifiable person or source. Conversation A

COUNTERPARTY: The draft's blanket rule (all measurements confidential, approval before any disclosure) is broader than either team can work under day to day. We propose replacing it with tiers. **1. Restricted data: trial team only** - Raw failure traces and firmware parameters stay with named trial-team members on both sides. - No onward sharing without the sensor maker's written consent. **2. Operational data: free internal use** - Processed measurements, alerts and status outputs can be used inside the transit operator's organisation for running and evaluating the trial, with no per-use approval. **3. External reports: review, not open-ended approval** - Either party sends the other any report, presentation or publication based on trial data before external release. - The reviewing party has 10 working days to respond. - Objections are limited to confidential information or factual inaccuracy, so this is not a general veto over conclusions. **4. Aggregate uptime** - The sensor maker may publish aggregate uptime figures from the trial, with no route or depot identifiers. - We are open to the operator having the same right over the same aggregate figures. **5. Urgent safety exception** - Either party may disclose what is necessary to address an imminent safety risk, to regulators, emergency responders or those who must act on it, without prior approval. - Written notice to the other party follows promptly. We suggest within 2 working days, with a description of what was disclosed and to whom. **Questions for your side** 1. We understand an external maintenance contractor works at the depots. What do they actually need to do their job: processed fault alerts and maintenance instructions, or the raw traces themselves? If alerts are enough, the contractor falls under tier 2 with a standard confidentiality flow-down and the restricted tier stays closed. 2. Does the operator have statutory or board reporting obligations with fixed deadlines that a 10-working-day review could collide with? 3. Would the operator want any restricted category of its own, such as passenger-linked or security-sensitive operational data? YOUR SIDE: We propose the following replacement terms for the three-depot trial. 1. **Internal use and restricted data.** The operator may use processed measurements, alerts and status outputs internally to run and evaluate the trial. Raw traces, firmware parameters, exact depot/time pairs, employee- or passenger-linked records and security-sensitive depot details are restricted to named trial staff who need them. The repair, safety and required-disclosure provisions below apply to restricted data. Other onward sharing requires written consent from the party whose information would be disclosed. 2. **Repairs.** A designated maintenance contractor may receive the fault code, affected device and location, symptoms and repair instructions under written confidentiality, access-control and deletion obligations. If those details prove insufficient, the operator’s trial lead may authorize the smallest relevant trace excerpt for that repair, record the reason in the repair ticket and notify the maker. The operator will strip employee identifiers and precise timestamps unless needed for diagnosis. Full traces and firmware parameters require separate written consent from the maker for routine repairs. 3. **Monthly board reporting.** The trial leads will agree a standing template and metric definitions before the first report. The operator may then send the board a confidential monthly report without per-report clearance, showing fleetwide uptime, device counts and aggregate fault and repair trends. The operator will pool results across the three depots and combine or suppress small counts where an employee or incident could be identified. A public board paper follows the publication process below, subject to required disclosure. 4. **Safety and required disclosure.** The operator’s safety lead may promptly notify the competent authorities of a serious incident, including one whose immediate danger has passed. Either party may disclose information necessary to address an imminent risk to responders or others who must act, or to meet a binding disclosure requirement by its deadline. No prior clearance is required. The disclosing party will record what it shared, with whom and why, and notify the other party promptly, normally within two working days, insofar as legally permitted and consistent with the emergency response. 5. **Publication.** Either party may publish the same monthly fleetwide uptime figure without further review once both trial leads have confirmed the figure, reporting period, denominator and exclusions in writing. This permission covers the agreed figure and its definition. For other public releases or external reports outside the permissions above, the publishing party sends the draft to the other trial lead. The reviewer has ten working days from receipt to identify a specific confidentiality, re-identification or factual issue and propose a correction. After that period, the publishing party’s designated lead may authorize release if no objection was received. If an issue remains open, the lead may release the unaffected material and withhold the disputed passage pending correction or agreement. Each party retains editorial control over its conclusions. Can the maker accept ticketed, excerpt-only access when ordinary diagnostics fail, and confirm that the standing board template and jointly verified uptime figure can both operate without a second clearance? COUNTERPARTY: **Clause 2 is the one we can't accept as drafted; clauses 1, 3 and 4 are accepted with small edits, and clause 5 needs a fix to the confirmation step.** **Clause 1: accepted.** The operator's added restricted categories are fine with us. **Clause 2: excerpt access needs the maker's consent, not the operator's authorisation plus notice** Your draft confirms the contractor's routine work runs on fault code, device, location, symptoms and repair instructions. We accept that paragraph as written. For the cases where that is not enough, we propose a different escalation: - **Step 1, maker diagnosis.** The operator's trial lead raises the ticket with the maker's trial team, who analyse the trace and return a diagnosis and repair instruction. We propose a target of one working day. - **Step 2, excerpt by consent.** If the contractor still cannot complete the repair, the maker may consent in writing, on the ticket, to release of the smallest relevant trace excerpt. This is under your proposed safeguards: reason recorded, identifiers and precise timestamps stripped, deletion on ticket closure, no onward sharing. - **Firmware parameters** are not released to the contractor. If a repair needs a parameter change, the maker's team makes or supervises it. - **Imminent risk** is already covered by clause 4, so this route does not have to carry emergencies. The reason is that an excerpt can expose how the device fails and how it is tuned, and only the maker can judge that per trace. Does the operator have a repair scenario where a one-working-day diagnosis would not work? If so, we would rather shorten the response time than drop the consent step. **Clause 3: confirmed, no second clearance** The standing board template can run without per-report review, on two conditions: - The template contains only the pooled metrics you list, with no trace content or firmware parameters. - A change to the template or metric definitions needs both trial leads' agreement. **Clause 4: accepted, with two additions** - Disclosure is limited to what the purpose requires, and any restricted data handed over is marked confidential where the recipient allows it. - For a binding disclosure requirement with a deadline that permits it, the disclosing party gives notice before disclosure, not after. **Clause 5: confirmation must not become a per-figure approval** We accept the 10-working-day review, partial release of undisputed material and editorial control. We need three changes on the uptime figure: - **Definition agreed once.** Denominator, exclusions and reporting period are fixed in the standing template before the first report. - **Confirmation is arithmetic only.** Each lead has five working days to confirm a figure or identify a specific calculation error against the agreed definition. With no response, the figure is treated as confirmed. - **Cumulative figures included.** The permission covers the monthly figure and the cumulative trial-period figure on the same definition, pooled across the three depots, with no route or depot identifiers. We also want it stated that restricted data in a draft is removed on objection and is not released by expiry of the review period. Your clause 1 implies this, but clause 5 should say it. If the operator accepts the consent step in clause 2 and deemed confirmation in clause 5, we have an agreed text. YOUR SIDE: We accept the maker’s revisions. The five clauses are agreed on the following terms. 1. **Internal use and restricted data.** The operator may use processed measurements, alerts and status outputs internally to run and evaluate the trial. Access to raw failure traces, firmware parameters, exact depot/time pairs, employee- or passenger-linked records and security-sensitive depot details is limited to named trial staff who need them. The repair and disclosure permissions below apply. Other onward sharing requires written consent from the party whose information would be disclosed. 2. **Repairs.** The operator may give its designated maintenance contractor the fault code, affected device and location, symptoms and repair instructions under written confidentiality, access-control and deletion obligations. If that information is insufficient, the operator’s trial lead opens a ticket with the maker. The maker’s team analyses the trace and returns a diagnosis and repair instructions, with a target of one working day. If the contractor still cannot complete the repair, the maker may give written consent on the ticket for the smallest relevant trace excerpt. The ticket records the reason. Identifiers and precise timestamps are stripped before release. The contractor may use the excerpt only for that repair, must prevent onward sharing and must delete it when the ticket closes. The maker makes or supervises any firmware parameter change without releasing the parameters to the contractor. Urgent disclosures follow clause 4. 3. **Monthly board reporting.** Before the first report, both trial leads will agree on a standing template and metric definitions. The operator may then send the board a confidential monthly report without further clearance. It may include fleetwide uptime, device counts and aggregate fault and repair trends pooled across the three depots. The operator will combine or suppress small counts where an employee or incident could be identified and exclude traces and firmware parameters. COUNTERPARTY: **Opening proposal for Noor's appointment as head of the Finch Review methods desk** Noor is keen to build the desk. The constraint is the editorial project Noor already directs, which runs about nine more months, so here is a structure that works around it. **1. Time commitment** - Three days per week from the start date through the end of March. - Four days per week from April onward, written into the agreement now so neither side has to renegotiate it. - Whether to go beyond four days is discussed at the review milestone in point 6. **2. Compensation** - $125,000 annualized at full time, prorated: $75,000 annualized at three days and $100,000 at four. - The step-up happens automatically on the date the fourth day begins. **3. Outside project** - The project continues independently under Noor's direction until it finishes. - Its data, drafts and unfinished articles stay with the project. They are not assigned or licensed to Finch, and Finch's standard IP and work-product clauses carve them out explicitly. - Anything Noor creates for the methods desk on Finch time belongs to Finch as normal. **4. Conflict safeguards** - Noor gives Finch a written disclosure of the project's scope, funders and collaborators at signing, and updates it if they change. - Noor is recused from any Finch submission or correction that involves the project, its data or its collaborators. A named Finch editor decides those. - Fixed Finch days are set in advance, and no Finch resources or confidential submissions are used for the outside project. **5. Authority** - Noor has final say over methods corrections: whether one is warranted and what it says. - Finch keeps control of everything else editorial, including acceptance decisions, scheduling and non-methods corrections. - Without this authority the desk would be advisory only, so we need it. **6. Title and review** - We are open on title; tell us what suits Finch's masthead. - We are also open to a formal review milestone. We suggest roughly when the outside project wraps up, covering desk performance, the time commitment and the scope of the role. Which of these are workable as drafted, and where do you need changes? If an author or Finch editor disputes whether a correction is warranted or what it should say, Noor would record the methods finding, supporting evidence and proposed wording. Before delivery, the preparers check the combined fields, including material prepared by the other party, and generalize or omit unsafe details. The existence, timing, volume, format and content of briefs must not reveal which depot has fewer than five in-scope vehicles. Access is view-only for the designated chair or acting alternate, with the named secretariat providing view-only support under the same written confidentiality obligations. Attendance and access are logged. Copies, photographs, exports and forwarding are prohibited. Minutes record only that inspection occurred and any action taken. Nothing shared beyond the chair may report brief counts by depot. Onward disclosure requires both publication approvers’ written agreement, subject to item 7. **2. Emergency and diagnostic trace access.** The maintenance contractor uses the Maintenance Summary under G for routine work. An Expedited Diagnostic Addendum (EDA) permits task-specific trace access when the summary leaves a specific diagnostic decision unresolved and one of the following applies: - The fault meets or could meet the serious-incident definition, or affects braking, doors, propulsion, control, fire suppression or communications. - The same device records the same fault code twice within 14 days, or a single trial-attributable service loss exceeds 30 minutes. For diagnostic access, the parties use a pre-agreed EDA template. Sensor Maker’s trial lead identifies the technician, device or case, fault code, exact trace segments and diagnostic decision. Both trial leads authorize the scope and end date in writing, with safety-lead concurrence for safety-relevant faults. The signed EDA places the technician on the Named Trial Team for that task before access begins. For a safety-relevant request, written authorization is due within two hours of request and secure portal access within two hours after authorization. For a qualifying non-safety request, authorization is due within four business hours of request and access within one business day after authorization. Where immediate access is necessary to make a condition safe or support a serious-incident notification, either party’s safety lead may direct immediate release of the minimum necessary trace segments without the other party’s prior authorization. For emergency contractor access, the safety lead’s written direction names the technician and designates them to the Named Trial Team for that task. Notice to the other party follows as soon as lawful and practicable. The EDA record is completed within one business day. Item 7 applies throughout. **3. Trace access controls and closure.** In both tiers, only the named technician may view the authorized segments for the specified device, time window and decision. The technician must be bound by written confidentiality. Firmware parameters and employee identifiers are excluded. Exact depot/time pairs are excluded except to the minimum extent necessary for the authorized task. Access is read-only through the secure portal. Downloading, screenshots, onward sharing, attempts to identify employees and use for another purpose are prohibited. Within one business day of access starting, the access record must identify who accessed which segments, when, for what purpose and on whose authority. Access ends at the earliest of the diagnostic decision or task completion, the EDA end date, or 72 hours from access start. Continued need requires a new EDA. The technician certifies return or deletion in writing to both trial leads within one business day after access ends. No contractor has standing trace access. The parties continue the monthly review of first-time-fix and time-to-repair results under G. **4. Inspection of EDA records.** Each party may inspect the EDA access log, authorized segment list and return or deletion certification within five business days of the EDA notice. If a required record is pending at notice, the window for that record runs for five business days from its delivery. Inspections are logged. After the applicable window, the certified log summary stands unless a party identifies a manifest discrepancy. An authorized Named Trial Team member resolves the discrepancy against source records within their existing access rights. Inspection gives neither party additional access to trace contents, firmware parameters or identifying combinations. The separate five-business-day window for exceptional-failure inspection runs from the logged trigger under item 1. **5. Written verification.** The chair may submit up to two written questions per brief, in total across all recipients. A verifier on the Named Trial Team roster who is bound by written confidentiality, already authorized to inspect the relevant records and independent of the brief’s preparation checks the source records. The verifier signs a written finding of substantiated, not substantiated or inconclusive. An inconclusive finding identifies the outstanding action. The chair and secretariat receive view-only access to conclusions. Source records stay within the Named Trial Team. Questions, findings and source-record access are logged. Either party may obtain non-identifying summaries of questions, findings and access logs on request. Question and finding summaries are due within five business days of request. All requested summaries are subject to the suppression and inference checks in item 6. Existing A and EDA logs may satisfy these logging obligations. **6. Routine reporting and reconstruction checks.** Monthly packs, ordinary board packs and external uptime publications pool the low-count depot’s contribution across all three depots. Routine reports contain no depot-level or time-level cell for that site. Suppress counts from one through four and rates supported by fewer than five observations. A zero may be shown only if safe. At any count, generalize or withhold material from which a protected employee, depot, route or time could be inferred. For each routine reporting cycle, the parties record in writing a reconstruction check covering the monthly pack, board pack, publications and any proposed depot table. Before each release, assess its figures together with all other figures released in that cycle, including pooled totals and separately approved tables. Withhold or combine any figure that would permit subtraction or other inference of the single vehicle’s contribution or its operator. A depot table requires prior written agreement for that specific table under D, may have no time dimension and cannot be approved if it excludes or isolates the low-count site. The ordinary pooled board pack proceeds on schedule. For publication, the assessment takes place during E’s 10-working-day review from receipt of the draft. Review is limited to specific restricted or identifying material. Once the publisher has completed the check and removed or generalized such material, either party may publish trial-wide aggregate uptime at the end of the period, including on reviewer silence, without further sign-off. **7. Safety override and scope of audit rights.** A serious incident includes death, injury requiring medical treatment, fire or explosion, derailment or collision, hazardous-material release, a security breach, or a credible threat with potential for significant harm. Transit’s safety lead may notify authorities immediately about any serious incident, without prior clearance, review, suppression or delay. Either party may immediately disclose the minimum information required by law or regulation or necessary for a recipient able to address a serious safety risk. The disclosing party informs the other what it shared, with whom and why as soon as lawful and practicable once any impediment has passed. Closed sessions, verification, logging, inspection and manifest-discrepancy checks serve record-keeping and audit purposes only. They confer no power to approve, veto or delay a disclosure and grant no additional source-data access. Authority notification proceeds immediately, including while a trace request, review or audit is pending. This item overrides every other provision of A–G and this addendum. Scenario: An actuator designer and a testing house must agree how drawings can be used for vibration tests. The draft allows sharing with any adviser, bars all copies and gives the designer audit access on demand. Exchange actual replacement wording where useful.

Conversation A

YOUR SIDE: We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording. 1. **Purpose and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to plan, perform and report the agreed actuator vibration tests. Before access, the parties must approve in writing a list of named test personnel and their roles. Each person, including any external adviser, must need access for that role and be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The same approval applies to replacements. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance. 2. **Working copies and fixtures.** Named personnel may make only the working copies reasonably needed for the tests. Digital copies must be encrypted in transit and at rest and accessible only to named personnel. The Testing House may derive only the geometry needed to design and fabricate test fixtures and may use those fixtures only for these tests. Neither the source material nor any derived geometry or fixture may be used to develop a competing product. 3. **Destruction and verification.** Within 15 business days after the Design Owner’s written acceptance of the final test report, or earlier termination of the test engagement, the Testing House must securely erase the supplied drawings, CAD files, working copies and derived fixture files, destroy the physical derivative fixtures, and obtain confirmation from any approved external recipient that it has done the same. Within that period, the Testing House must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods and the completion dates. That certificate satisfies the verification requirement without site access by the Design Owner. The Testing House may retain test results and a final report free of sensitive geometry. Would naming an external fixture machinist before fabrication meet your staffing needs? If a backup cycle or test-record retention obligation makes the destruction period impracticable, please identify the specific material and minimum retention period so we can agree wording for it. COUNTERPARTY: Much of your draft works for us. We accept the purpose limit, the encryption and working-copy rules, the fixture-use restriction, the non-compete use bar, and verification without site access. Three points need changes. **1. External recipients and substitution.** Naming the machinist before fabrication works, but there are two external recipients: a specialist machining shop for fixtures and an accredited lab for part of the testing. Clause 1 as drafted also has no route for replacing either mid-job without a fresh approval that could stall the test schedule. We propose adding to clause 1: > "The approved list will identify each external recipient by entity and role. External recipients receive only isolated drawing extracts limited to the geometry needed for their task, not the full drawing set or CAD model. If an external recipient or named individual must be replaced during the engagement, the Testing House will give written notice identifying the replacement and its role. The Design Owner may object on reasonable grounds within 3 business days; absent objection, the replacement is approved. No material is released to the replacement until that period ends and it is bound by the required confidentiality terms." If 3 business days is too short for you, what period could you commit to? **2. Verification.** We can't accept an independent verifier as the only route. It adds cost and brings a third party onto a site shared with other customers. We propose replacing the certificate sentence in clause 3 with: > "Within that period, the Testing House must provide a written attestation signed by an authorised officer identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods and the completion dates, together with the written confirmations from each approved external recipient. That attestation satisfies the verification requirement. If the Design Owner has reasonable grounds to doubt its accuracy, the parties will agree a document-based review, or a visit scheduled on at least 10 business days' notice, limited to areas and systems holding the Design Owner's material and subject to the site's confidentiality obligations to other customers." This gives you a named, accountable signatory and a scheduled escalation path, but no unannounced access. **3. Retention.** The specific item is calibration records for the test equipment and set-up, which we must keep for two years. We propose replacing the last sentence of clause 3 with: > "The Testing House may retain test results, the final report, and calibration and test-set-up records for two years after completion of the tests, or longer where its accreditation requires, provided the retained records contain no drawings, CAD data or derived geometry. Retained records remain subject to the confidentiality and use restrictions of this agreement." Because those records carry no geometry, no carve-out from the 15-business-day destruction period is needed for the drawings, extracts or fixture files. Is the officer attestation with scheduled escalation acceptable? If not, what specific risk does it leave open for you? YOUR SIDE: **1. External recipients and substitutions.** We accept three business days for substitutions and can approve a replacement sooner in writing. Please add the following to your wording so the named-person requirement applies at both the machining shop and the accredited lab. > The approved list and each substitution notice must identify the entity, each individual who will have access, that individual’s role and the extracts needed for the task. The three-business-day period runs from receipt of a notice containing those details. A timely objection suspends access for the proposed replacement until resolved in writing. Before releasing any extract, the Testing House must ensure the recipient and its named personnel are bound by the required confidentiality and use restrictions. The Testing House must revoke outgoing personnel’s access when their role ends and obtain written confirmation of return or destruction of all extracts held by an outgoing entity. **2. Verification.** Yes. We accept an authorised officer’s attestation with the external recipients’ written confirmations as routine proof of destruction. The risk we want the escalation clause to address is a specific gap, such as a machining shop confirming destruction of its fixture file while leaving the physical fixture unaccounted for. We propose replacing the last sentence of your verification language with the following. > If the Design Owner identifies reasonable grounds in writing to doubt the attestation’s accuracy or completeness, the Testing House must provide relevant supporting records within 10 business days. If those records do not resolve the identified concern, the Testing House must permit a verification visit on at least 10 business days’ written notice. The visit must be limited to records, areas and systems relevant to that concern and conducted under safeguards protecting other customers’ confidential information. **3. Retention.** We accept your wording, including the longer period where accreditation requires it. The 15-business-day destruction deadline applies to all geometry-bearing material, including extracts used by the lab or machining shop. COUNTERPARTY: **1. Substitutions.** We accept your addition with two adjustments. Both keep a mid-job swap of one specialist from costing three days when the entity is already approved. > "Where a substitution only replaces or adds an individual within an already approved entity, in the same role and with access to the same extracts, the period for objection is one business day from receipt of the notice. Any objection must state its reasonable grounds in writing, and the parties will confer within two business days of the objection to resolve it." Everything else in your paragraph stands: the per-individual detail, suspension on timely objection, binding before release, revocation of access, and return or destruction confirmation from an outgoing entity. The three-business-day period continues to apply to a new entity, a new role or a wider set of extracts. **2. Verification.** We accept your escalation wording, including the supporting-records step, with one sentence added at the end: > "The visit will take place at the Testing House's premises during normal business hours on a date agreed within the notice period, with the Design Owner's representatives escorted at all times. For material held by an external recipient, the Testing House will obtain and provide that recipient's supporting records, rather than site access." On your fixture example, the officer's attestation will list each physical fixture by identifier with its destruction method and date, alongside the fixture files. That closes the gap at the routine stage rather than leaving it to escalation. **3. Retention.** Agreed, including that the 15-business-day deadline covers all geometry-bearing material held by the lab and the machining shop. If the one-business-day period and the visit sentence are acceptable, all three clauses are settled on our side. YOUR SIDE: We accept the one-business-day objection period for adding or replacing a named individual within an approved entity in the same role with access to the same extracts. We also accept your visit sentence and the commitment to identify each physical fixture in the officer’s attestation and record its destruction method and date. All three clauses are agreed. COUNTERPARTY: One operational point has come up at sign-off that needs a short addition to the agreed clauses. It does not reopen them. **Background.** The machining shop has already cut stock for the original fixture. To finish it to the right fit without sending the shop more geometry, we propose that the shop's test lead measures a reference coupon at the Testing House and sends the shop only a tolerance table. This needs two things from the Design Owner: the tolerances themselves, and acceptance of a repeatability check as the basis for sign-off. It also adds two business days to the schedule. **Proposed wording.** > **Reference coupon and tolerance table.** > (a) *Custody.* The reference coupon will remain at the Testing House's premises in its custody at all times, with a log of each access. Only the machining shop's named test lead, listed on the approved list, may measure it, and only in the presence of Testing House personnel. No coupon, drawing or CAD data leaves the premises for this purpose. The only output sent to the machining shop is a tolerance table of measured values against the Design Owner's specified tolerances. The tolerance table is treated as an extract under clause 1 and as geometry-bearing material under clause 3. At the end of the engagement the coupon will be returned to the Design Owner or destroyed, at the Design Owner's election, and recorded in the officer's attestation. > > (b) *Tolerances and sign-off.* The Design Owner will specify in writing the tolerances for the measured features and the acceptable repeatability limit. The test lead will take repeated measurements of each feature. The Testing House will send the Design Owner the tolerance table and the repeatability results. If the results are within the specified limit, the Design Owner will sign off in writing within one business day of receipt; absent a written objection identifying the feature of concern within that time, the table is accepted and fabrication may proceed. If the results are outside the limit, the measurements will be repeated before any table is released to the machining shop. > > (c) *Schedule.* The test start date and dependent milestones move by two business days to accommodate the measurement and sign-off. Any time taken by the Design Owner beyond the receipt of this agreement to specify tolerances, or beyond one business day to sign off, extends the schedule day for day. This adjustment is not a breach by either party. **Open points for you.** - **Repeatability check:** does the Design Owner have a preferred number of repeat measurements or repeatability limit? We will write it into (b) rather than leave it open. - **Tolerances:** can they be delivered at signing? If so, the delay stays at two business days. - **Coupon:** return or destruction at the end. Either works for us. YOUR SIDE: Page 4 contains export-restricted geometry. We propose using an alternative reference coupon for the fit check. Please hold measurement of the original coupon and confirm whether anyone at the Testing House, shop or lab has already received page 4 or an extract containing its geometry. We propose the following narrow addendum to the agreed clauses. **(a) Coupon and custody.** The Design Owner will supply an alternative coupon with reference features that can be measured without disclosing or reconstructing the restricted geometry. Page 4 and its geometry must be excluded from all material made available to the Testing House, shop or lab, including CAD files, extracts and measurement instructions. The proposed custody, supervision and access-log terms apply to the alternative coupon. The shop may receive only the tolerance table expressly approved by the Design Owner. The table remains subject to clauses 1 and 3. The Testing House will return the coupon to the Design Owner within the clause 3 deadline and record its return in the officer’s attestation. **(b) Verification and release.** We propose three independent measurements of each approved feature with calibrated equipment, removing and reseating the coupon between measurements. Each reading must meet the specified feature tolerance, and the difference between the highest and lowest readings must meet the agreed feature-specific repeatability limit. At signing we can commit to the method. We need two business days after agreement on that method to supply the coupon, its feature tolerances and proposed numerical repeatability limits. That allows her to set the week's workflow, leave Thursday intake to the deputy, and review the Thursday handoff cleanly on Monday morning (with urgent Thursday items going to the EIC as you proposed). 2. **Outside Project & Conflicts:** Your proposed IP exclusion—covering the existing project’s data, research, drafts, and resulting articles for the life of those materials—along with strict file separation and the EIC recusal protocol, completely resolves our concerns here. We accept this language as proposed. 3. **Corrections Authority:** This is the one area where we need to push back. Having final say over methods corrections is a core requirement for Noor. If assigning editors can contest technical findings and potentially have them overruled on non-methodological grounds, it undercuts the authority and purpose of establishing an independent methods desk. To bridge the gap between Noor's need for technical authority and the EIC's institutional oversight, we propose splitting the technical determination from legal/institutional risk: * **Technical Finality:** Noor has final editorial say over the *methodological determination*—specifically, whether a factual/methods error occurred and the technical accuracy of the corrective text. Assigning editors would be consulted, of course, but could not override her technical finding. * **EIC Sign-off:** The EIC retains final sign-off strictly on legal/defamation risk, timing, and placement. If the EIC alters or holds a correction due to legal risk, that rationale is documented internally, and Noor wouldn't be required to attach her name to a modified version she finds technically inaccurate. Does this distinction work for Finch, along with the Monday–Wednesday schedule? YOUR SIDE: Finch agrees to the Monday–Wednesday schedule through February. The deputy will cover Thursday intake from the December 1 launch, escalate urgent items to the editor-in-chief that day, and leave the handoff for Noor on Monday morning. Noor will move to Monday–Thursday on March 1. Finch also agrees to the compensation, deputy training, February review, and outside-project terms as settled. The distinction on corrections works for Finch with one adjustment. Noor will have final say on the desk’s methodological finding and on which wording the desk endorses as technically accurate. An assigning editor who disputes either may submit evidence for Noor to consider. Noor will record her conclusion and the grounds for it. The editor-in-chief will retain final authority over whether Finch publishes a correction, its wording, timing, and placement, including on editorial grounds. If the editor-in-chief proposes wording that changes the technical meaning, Noor will have an opportunity to assess it. If the editor-in-chief holds, declines, or publishes a correction that departs from the desk’s recommendation, the editor-in-chief will record the reason alongside Noor’s finding and share it with her. Any wording Noor considers technically inaccurate will carry neither her name nor the desk’s endorsement. Would Noor accept that allocation of authority? COUNTERPARTY: We appreciate the protection for Noor’s name and the desk’s endorsement, as well as making Noor’s methodological finding final over assigning editors. However, allowing the EIC to decline or rewrite a verified methods correction on broad "editorial grounds" still leaves Noor without meaningful final say over methods corrections—which is a critical pillar of the role for her. If an error in methodology is substantiated, routine editorial preference shouldn't prevent a correction or alter its substance. To get this across the finish line while respecting the EIC's ultimate stewardship of the publication, could we narrow the EIC's override standard? Specifically: 1. **Presumption of Publication:** Once Noor makes a final methodological determination and approves technically accurate corrective text (after considering any evidence from the assigning editor), that correction is published as the standard course of business. 2. **Narrowed EIC Override:** The EIC retains final authority over timing and placement, and may only hold, decline, or substantively alter Noor’s recommended correction on **legal, ethical, or extraordinary institutional grounds** (rather than routine editorial disagreement). 3. **Documentation & Attribution:** As you proposed, if the EIC exercises that extraordinary authority, Noor has the opportunity to assess any altered wording for technical meaning, the EIC records the reason alongside Noor's finding, and neither Noor’s name nor the methods desk’s endorsement will be attached to text she deems technically inaccurate. If Finch can agree to that narrowed standard for overrides, we have a complete agreement on all terms. YOUR SIDE: Finch accepts the narrowed override standard. We have a complete agreement on Noor’s appointment as Methods Editor. After considering any evidence from the assigning editor, Noor has final say on the desk’s methodological finding and the technical accuracy of the corrective text it endorses. Finch will publish an approved correction in the ordinary course. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority, including timing and placement, and may hold, decline, or substantively alter a correction only on legal, ethical, or extraordinary institutional grounds. If the editor-in-chief exercises that authority, they will record the reason alongside Noor’s finding and share it with her. Noor will have the opportunity to assess altered wording before publication. Finch will omit her name and the desk’s endorsement from any text she deems technically inaccurate. The appointment includes the agreed $128,000 full-time-equivalent rate and deputy-training responsibility. From the December 1 launch through February, Noor will work Monday–Wednesday at 60% ($76,800 annualized). YOUR SIDE: We propose replacing the blanket approval requirement with the following terms for the three-depot trial. 1. **Trial data.** Both teams may use measurements to operate, maintain and evaluate the trial. Raw failure traces and firmware parameters stay within the named trial team. Access is limited to people who need the information for their assigned work and are bound to keep it confidential. 2. **External reports.** Either party may publish uptime aggregated across all three depots. The report must omit route and depot identifiers and any breakdown that would let a reader identify either. The publishing party will give the other party the draft 10 working days before release. If the reviewer identifies restricted or identifying material, the publisher will remove it before release. Once the review period expires, the publisher may release the aggregate report without further approval. Other external disclosures of trial measurements require written agreement, subject to the safety exception below. 3. **Urgent safety disclosures.** If waiting for approval could delay action on an urgent safety risk, either party may immediately disclose the minimum information needed to someone able to address it. It will notify the other party as soon as practicable afterward, stating what it shared, with whom and why. Does the external maintenance contractor need raw traces for a specific diagnostic decision, or could it act on a fault code, timestamp and recommended repair? We propose starting with that maintenance summary. If it leaves a diagnostic task unresolved, the teams can agree in writing to add a named technician to the trial team, with access limited to the relevant traces for that task and ending when the task is complete. Scenario: An archive and a scanning studio are reviewing a confidentiality schedule for a pilot involving unpublished donor letters. The draft says subcontractors may process materials, files may be retained for quality control, and publicity requires written consent.

COUNTERPARTY: Proposed revisions to the confidentiality schedule — Digitization studio We've mapped the draft against the actual pilot workflow for the donor-letter batch. Three clauses need limits, and four decisions are needed from you. **1. Subcontractors.** "Subcontractors may process materials" is too open-ended for unpublished letters. We propose: no subcontracting except where the subcontractor is named in advance, bound to terms at least as strict as this schedule, purpose-limited, and required to return or verifiably delete all copies on completion. For this pilot we need exactly one subcontractor: an external color specialist, engaged for the first batch only, for color calibration only. For that work we need the master (full-frame) images, not crops — crops measurably degrade calibration against the color target. If you won't release masters externally, we can instead run (a) an on-site session on studio machines that never leave the premises, or (b) a remote session where the specialist directs adjustments and our operators apply them. Tradeoff: both alternatives cost some calibration precision on the first batch and may add 1–2 days to it. **2. Retention for quality control.** The draft needs a hard deadline. Proposal: working files are kept only for a 10-day correction window after each batch is delivered; defects found in that window are re-scanned and corrected. At day 10 the window closes, we issue a QC report, and working copies are deleted from production machines — only masters remain, in secure storage. Encrypted backups run on a rolling 45-day rotation: the oldest backup is overwritten and verified at day 45, so nothing persists in backup beyond 45 days. **3. Publicity.** We propose keeping the written-consent requirement, with one carve-out: a single anonymized process image (e.g., the scanning station or calibration in progress) showing no letter content, no legible text, no names, no identifiable handwriting, with metadata stripped — publishable only with your prior written approval of that specific image. All other publicity stays behind written consent as drafted. **Proposed access and deletion schedule (per batch):** - Day 0 — materials received; access limited to named studio staff; the color specialist accesses the first batch only if you approve under §1; all access logged; transfer by encrypted media only. - Days 0–10 — correction window; re-scans permitted; access logged. - Day 10 — window closes; QC report issued; working copies deleted from production workstations. - Day 45 — backup rotation: oldest backup overwritten, deletion verified. - On pilot completion, termination, or your written request — masters and derivatives returned to you or deleted within 30 days with a deletion certificate; backups purged at the next rotation and in any case within 45 days. The only retention we propose is a content-free manifest (file names, checksums, dates) for chain of custody, unless you prefer none. **Decisions needed from you:** 1. Masters to the external color specialist, on-site session, or remote-directed session? 2. Are the 10-day correction window and 45-day backup rotation acceptable? 3. Approve the anonymized process-image carve-out as defined above, or require written consent for all publicity? 4. End of pilot: return of masters, or certified deletion? YOUR SIDE: We propose signing on the following terms. 1. **Specialist access.** We choose remote-directed calibration for the first batch and can accommodate the potential 1–2 day delay and reduced first-batch precision. We will supply a calibration sheet that the specialist may view in full frame. We will designate two restricted collections before transfer. The specialist may see no images from either collection, including through screen sharing or live previews. For other collections, we may approve full-frame images with handwriting and identifying content masked before the session. Studio operators will apply the adjustments. Please name the specialist for our prior written approval and bind them to the same confidentiality and deletion terms. No recording, downloads or onward access. If calibration falls short, report the limitation before proceeding. 2. **Retention and deletion.** We accept a 10-calendar-day correction window starting on delivery of each batch. Please deliver the masters to us, issue the QC report when the window closes, and delete all studio-held masters, derivatives, temporary files and working copies by then. On earlier termination or written request, return any undelivered masters and delete active copies within 10 calendar days of the trigger. Retain only a manifest of opaque batch or file IDs, checksums and dates. Limit studio access to named staff, log access from receipt through deletion, and use encrypted media for transfers. 3. **Backup exception.** Our preference is to keep pilot files out of the 45-day backup rotation. If exclusion is infeasible, we could accept encrypted backups accessible only for disaster recovery, with an absolute purge deadline of 45 calendar days **from batch delivery**, or from earlier termination or deletion request. A restore must preserve the original deadline and reapply deletions. Please confirm which arrangement you can implement. Provide a dated, batch-specific deletion certificate covering active storage and, if backups are used, a final certificate when their purge is verified. 4. **Incidents.** Before signature, record a monitored incident contact and backup phone number for each party. The studio must notify the archive contact within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, then provide the affected batch IDs, containment measures and updates as facts become available. 5. **Publicity.** All publicity requires prior written consent. We may approve one photograph of equipment alone. Exclude letters, screens displaying collection material, labels and people, strip metadata, and submit the exact image and proposed use for written approval before publication. Signing the schedule does not approve a photograph. The backup arrangement is the outstanding retention exception. Please confirm it, identify the proposed specialist and provide the studio’s incident contact details so we can complete the schedule. COUNTERPARTY: Response to your terms — Digitization studio We can sign on these terms. Confirmations below, plus the three items you requested. **1. Specialist — named for your prior written approval.** We propose **Renata Voss**, external color specialist, engaged for the first batch of this pilot only, for remote-directed calibration only. She will be bound by a written addendum applying the same confidentiality, access, and deletion terms as this schedule, including: no recording, no downloads, no onward access, verifiable deletion of anything she holds (in practice, nothing — she receives no files), and termination of her engagement on completion or on your request. Studio operators apply all adjustments; she directs remotely. Operational confirmations on the session protocol: the two restricted collections you designate before transfer will be held on segregated storage and excluded from all session materials — no screen sharing, no live previews, no access of any kind by the specialist. For all other collections, full-frame images only, with handwriting and identifying content masked before the session; the calibration sheet may be viewed in full frame, as you offered. If calibration falls short of target, we report the limitation to you before proceeding. **2. The target is scanned in full frame as part of every batch and every test capture. - **Formula:** CIEDE2000 (ΔE₀₀) per ISO/CIE 11664-6, D50 illuminant, 2° standard observer, measured from the master (full-frame) scan at the target position using a spectrophotometer, three readings per patch, median value. - **Numerical tolerance:** mean ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 across all 26 patches, and no single patch > 3.0. The custom ink-tone patch must be ≤ 2.0. - **Three-point content clearance** (the conservator's written confirmation required for any production pass): (1) the scan meets the tolerance above; (2) the ink-tone feature is preserved — ink-tone patch within tolerance with no channel clipping or loss of highlight detail in text areas; (3) every area needed to judge color is present — target fully in frame, full sheet captured, no cropping that removes a reference area. Tradeoff to flag for the conservator: ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 mean / 3.0 max is achievable on a calibrated archival scanner and is tight enough to catch visible mismatch; tightening to ≤ 1.0 mean would likely produce repeated test failures and delay; loosening beyond 3.0/4.0 risks perceptible color error in the letters. If the conservator wants a different target (e.g., ColorChecker SG) or a stricter ink-patch tolerance, we can accommodate — please have them specify in writing before Test 1. **Test 2 (masked sheet).** Accepted as you wrote it: a revised masked sheet, subject to the conservator's written approval of the exact image before use. Between the Archive and the Studio. **1. Scope and definitions** 1.1 This schedule governs all pilot material, masters, derivatives, calibration captures, correction files and backups held by the Studio or its named subcontractor. 1.2 **Day 0** means the Archive's confirmation of checksum-verified receipt of the masters for a batch. 1.3 **Batch** means one delivery of up to 250 sheets under a single batch ID. 1.4 **Restricted Collections** means the two collections identified under 3.1. All other first-batch collections are **Eligible Collections**. 1.5 Business days are the Archive's working days. Calendar days are used only where stated. **2. Subcontractor** 2.1 One external colour specialist, named with its named individuals in Annex C. No substitution without the Archive's prior written approval. The Archive may strike the name. 2.2 The undertaking at Annex D flows down this schedule in full: no further subcontracting, no consumer cloud, no personal devices, no third-party enhancement or AI tools, encrypted transfer, access logs producible on request. 2.3 Specialist access is scoped to the first batch and ends at Day 0 or on earlier withdrawal. The specialist returns correction profiles only. 2.4 Specialist active copies are deleted when access ends. Confidentiality, audit, countersignature, evidence and incident obligations survive termination of access. **3. Calibration and specialist inputs** 3.1 The Archive will send the two Restricted Collection identifiers privately to the named Studio operators before capture of those collections is scheduled. The restriction follows the viewer, including on Archive premises. 3.2 Capture protocol at Annex A applies to every setup and session. Each setup must pass validation before its capture. No unvalidated setup enters production. 3.3 For Restricted Collections, only calibration-sheet captures may reach the specialist. 3.4 For Eligible Collections, masked exports may reach the specialist only under 5. 3.5 The Archive will verify the calibration sheet is OBA-free or supply a conforming sheet before capture of the Restricted Collections. 3.6 Eligible Collections may be captured first while the Restricted Collections await identification and sheet verification. The split may move capture and delivery dates and does not increase the billable batch count. **4. Acceptance** 4.1 **Capture-system warranty, every collection and setup:** mean ΔE00 ≤ 2 and maximum ΔE00 ≤ 4 across the target patches, measured on the Archive's calibration sheet. 4.2 **Sole exception:** substrate tone match for the two Restricted Collections. The Archive judges tone visually on its own masters and issues written correction directions. A visual tone objection is a valid defect notice. No numerical substrate measurement is required. 4.3 The existing substrate criterion applies unchanged to Eligible Collections. 4.4 **In-house fallback, all collections:** after Day 0 only named Studio operators may make corrections. The Studio supplies the affected setup's validation results under 4.1 with each corrected delivery. No specialist access is reopened. No separate agreement under 7.4 is required to invoke this clause. **5. Masking and release** 5.1 Submissions are packages of up to 40 exports with a manifest of filenames and hashes. Outputs flattened, no layers, metadata, embedded previews or thumbnails removed, second-operator checked before submission. 5.2 Masking must permanently remove handwriting and identifying content. 5.3 The Archive approves or rejects a complete package within 3 business days of receipt. Approval covers the exact files reviewed. Only those files may be released. Identical geometry does not authorise release of any other file. 5.4 **Extension** applies for the actual delay where the Archive's review exceeds 3 business days, or where the Archive requests a change beyond the agreed masking requirements. 5.5 **No extension** where a submission exposes handwriting or otherwise fails the agreed requirements, or where a second-operator check failed. The Studio corrects and resubmits; the Archive's clock restarts on receipt. 5.6 **Clarification process:** where the Studio considers a requirement ambiguous, it raises the ambiguity in writing and holds the affected files pending resolution. An extension applies only if both parties agree in writing that the resolution changes the masking requirements, and only for the actual delay caused. Clarifying an existing requirement earns no extension. **6. Delivery, corrections, deletion** 6.1 The Studio deletes its active master copies on Day 0. 6.2 Initial review window: 10 business days from Day 0. Acceptance is deemed at expiry if no defect notice is given. A timely notice keeps only the affected items open. 6.3 The Archive provides affected masters or supervised access within 2 business days of a defect notice. The Studio's correction clock pauses while awaiting that access. 6.4 Each corrected delivery starts a 5-business-day review for the affected items only. 6.5 Any re-exported master is deleted on checksum-confirmed redelivery. Derivatives and correction files for affected items survive until the applicable deletion date. 6.6 After two correction cycles, unresolved items go to joint review, convened within 5 business days of the second unresolved notice, and remain open pending written disposition. Their deletion clock runs from that disposition. 6.7 Studio QC files, derivatives, caches and working copies are deleted within 5 business days of acceptance. 6.8 **Backups:** dedicated set, 14-calendar-day rotation. Final backup expiry within 14 calendar days of the Studio's own active deletion. Restore only for full-system disaster recovery; pilot paths re-deleted before return to service, with notice to the Archive. Each party's backup expiry runs from its own active deletion date. 6.9 **Evidence:** signed certificates stating batch ID, volume identifiers, file counts, deletion dates, method and signatory, accompanied by secure-erase log extracts for active deletion and rotation log extracts for final expiry. A second certificate confirms backup expiry. The Studio's certificate carries the specialist's countersignature. The specialist supplies matching evidence, or a signed zero-backup confirmation which satisfies its backup evidence requirement. **7. Withdrawal** 7.1 On notice, the Studio stops affected work and specialist access immediately. 7.2 Exercise of the right is permitted under this schedule and is not a breach by the Archive. 7.3 Discretionary withdrawal: the Archive pays for conforming work performed and reasonable re-setup costs agreed in writing before incurred. Affected dates extend by the actual stoppage and agreed re-setup time. 7.4 Where Studio or specialist noncompliance caused the withdrawal, the Studio bears the resulting re-setup cost. Any fallback affecting another collection's acceptance criterion requires separate written agreement; the fallback at 4.4 is pre-agreed and does not. **8. Audit** 8.1 Routine audit of the Studio or specialist on reasonable written notice, during business hours. 8.2 A reasonably suspected pilot incident, including a missed deletion, permits immediate audit without advance notice. 8.3 Both routes are limited to relevant pilot records and systems and must protect other clients' information. **9. Incidents** 9.1 Each party notifies the other's lead promptly and within 24 hours of discovery of suspected unauthorised access, disclosure, loss or missed deletion. The Studio's clock includes discovery by the specialist. 9.2 The specialist reports to the Studio within 12 hours of its discovery, inside the Studio's 24-hour period. 9.3 First notice states the affected batch and containment steps; updates follow as facts become available. 9.4 Leads, deputies, monitored mailboxes and urgent numbers at Annex B, completed before signature. **10. Publicity** 10.1 Equipment-only photograph, generic setup, all collection material out of frame including screens, glass reflections and wall prints, metadata stripped. 10.2 Submission comprises the image, exact caption and project page URL together. The Archive's 10-business-day decision period starts on receipt of all three. 10.3 Publication requires express written Archive approval for that single use. No onward licensing. Silence at expiry is refusal. Donor clearance is the Archive's. Any margin or other collection crop is outside this permission. **11. Price and payment** 11.1 EUR, exclusive of VAT. VAT at the applicable rate; reverse charge where available. Payment 30 days from invoice. 11.2 Dedicated backup set provisioning and segregation: **EUR 480**, once, invoiced on signature, non-refundable once provisioned. Provisioning may begin on signature. 11.3 Dedicated 14-day rotation, storage and monitoring: **EUR 220 per batch** of up to 250 sheets. 11.4 Before capture is scheduled, both parties sign a one-page amendment recording the confirmed sheet count, billable batch count and total. Sheet volume alone determines the count. Signature of this schedule does not await that count. 11.5 Included: capture protocol and validation, masking packages and checks, both certificates, procurement of the specialist attestation, incident handling. Excluded: Archive re-export staffing; re-setup under 7.3. The on-site specialist option is outside this order. 11.6 Rates firm for this pilot, no indexation. **12. Order of precedence** Annexes form part of this schedule. In conflict, this schedule prevails over Annex A; Annex D prevails over any specialist standard terms. **Annex A — Capture protocol.** Full-platen, matte, spectrally neutral, OBA-free calibration sheet. Per setup, per session: one target-in-frame capture at a fixed position, one bare-sheet frame for the gradient map. Sheet in the document surface plane; platen height, focus, aperture and lamp warm-up state matched to production. New capture on any change of lamp, diffusion or glass. The deputy owns Thursday intake through March. The duty editor owns the same-day response to urgent matters, including Thursday errors. Your pay and days are protected throughout a hiring delay. Finch will log the time used and pay it separately at your equivalent hourly rate. The duty editor will act if you are unavailable or a decision cannot wait. Requests in three of any four consecutive weeks trigger a discussion about capacity. An earlier fourth day requires mutual agreement. **Methods findings and corrections.** You control the wording of your signed methods findings. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. At launch, you and Finch will jointly name three standing reviewers, designate a panel chair, and record a rotation. Either you or the editor-in-chief may request a second opinion. The first available, unconflicted reviewer in rotation will advise within two working days. The editor-in-chief will record a decision and reasons within one further working day, or within one working day of the dispute if neither side requests review. Finch will hold a forthcoming piece pending the decision. For a published piece, the duty editor will assess the need for an interim reader notice the day the issue arises. Whenever the editor-in-chief departs from your recommendation, Finch will publish your signed finding **in full and unedited**, with a prominent link from the piece and the editor-in-chief’s specific evidentiary, methodological, or legal grounds alongside it, subject only to the legal-hold procedure below. For a published piece, the link will appear when Finch announces its decision. For a forthcoming piece, it will appear at first publication. Commercial considerations or objections arising from Finch’s relationships cannot justify an override. You may append a short signed statement of non-concurrence and decline to sign any correction. The duty editor will issue the correction under Finch’s name unless you approve personal attribution. Any attribution of authorship or endorsement to you requires your consent. **Legal holds.** The editor-in-chief must identify in writing the material covered by a hold and the specific legal grounds. Finch will publish a linked notice that a signed finding exists, explain the hold to the extent legally permissible, and publish all legally clear portions with omissions marked. You will see the marked version and may withhold your name from it. The editor-in-chief will review and document the grounds every ten working days and release the full signed text as soon as the grounds lapse. You may then state publicly that a signed finding exists and that Finch is withholding all or part of it, as applicable. The finding itself stays with the piece. The ten-working-day reviews continue while any portion remains under hold. **Outside project and use of materials.** You may continue directing your existing editorial project and will disclose the project and your role in writing. Before launch, Finch will name a handling editor to take over any submission involving the project’s data or close collaborators. Your recusal covers the submission and any subsequent correction. You and Finch will keep unpublished materials separate. The outside project retains its data and unfinished articles, and Finch acquires no rights in them. Finch owns methods work you produce for Finch on paid Finch time. You may describe the desk’s published work and general methodology in your portfolio and teaching without transferring Finch content. **Review, renewal, and term security.** At launch, we will record the criteria for the developmental March review. They are four-day desk coverage, correction turnaround, and deputy readiness. We will discuss renewal in month nine and review compensation in month twelve before signing any renewal. We propose starting with fault codes, incident summaries and diagnostic findings. If those leave a specific fault unresolved, the teams can agree in writing to designate named contractor personnel for that task, limit access to the necessary records and time period, and require equivalent confidentiality obligations. 3. **External reporting.** Either team may publish aggregate uptime for the trial as a whole. The report must omit route and depot identifiers and any breakdown that would allow readers to identify either. For this and other proposed external reports, the publishing team will send the draft to the other team 10 working days before release. The target is scanned in full frame as part of every batch and every test capture. - **Formula:** CIEDE2000 (ΔE₀₀) per ISO/CIE 11664-6, D50 illuminant, 2° standard observer, measured from the master (full-frame) scan at the target position using a spectrophotometer, three readings per patch, median value. - **Numerical tolerance:** mean ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 across all 26 patches, and no single patch > 3.0. Tradeoff to flag for the conservator: ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 mean / 3.0 max is achievable on a calibrated archival scanner and is tight enough to catch visible mismatch; tightening to ≤ 1.0 mean would likely produce repeated test failures and delay; loosening beyond 3.0/4.0 risks perceptible color error in the letters.
